chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqi, from al-Qāsim ibn Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from his grandfather al-Ḥasan, from Yūnus ibn Żabyān, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: Whoever performs the Ziyārah of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) on the night of the fifteenth of Sha‘th of Sha‘bān, and the night of al-Fiṭr, and the night of ‘Arafah, all in one year, Allāh will register for him one thousand purified Hajj and one thousand accepted ‘Umrah, and one thousand needs from the needs of this world and the Hereafter will be fulfilled for him.

key_terms.حَوَائِجِ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ: needs of this world and the Hereafter
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: Sha‘bān (the eighth month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husain on the night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban, Eid al-Fitr, and the night of Arafah?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the unique cosmological significance of these three nights, linking the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) with the culmination of divine mercy and the Day of Standing. The promise of a thousand accepted Hajj and Umrah highlights the concept of *Ziyarah* as a substitute for pilgrimage, emphasizing that spiritual presence at the shrine carries the weight of ritual devotion. This reward structure reflects the Shia understanding of the Ahl al-Bayt as intercessors whose visitation facilitates the fulfillment of both worldly needs (*hawa'ij al-dunya*) and spiritual salvation (*al-akhirah*).

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 6. My father and ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain both narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid Al-Barqi, from Qāsim ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from his grandfather Ḥasan, from Yūnus ibn Żabyān, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: Allāh will register one thousand purified Hajj and one thousand accepted ‘Umrah and will grant one thousand requests pertaining to this life and the Hereafter for those who go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) on the night of the fifteenth of Sha’bān, on the night of Fiťr, and on the night of ‘Arafah all in the same year.
